problem: Decomposing complex natural images into separate layers with occlusion is difficult because existing methods struggle with occlusion completion, layer disentanglement, and precise foreground boundaries.
approach: RevealLayer uses a diffusion-based framework with region-aware attention to disentangle layers, an occlusion-guided adapter to enhance overlapping regions, and a composite loss to enforce sharp alpha boundaries.
contribution: The method outperforms existing approaches in layer decomposition and is supported by RevealLayer-100K, a high-quality multi-layer natural image dataset, and RevealLayerBench for benchmarking.

problem: Time series forecasting fails when patches contain low-quality information from missing values, distribution shifts, anomalies, or noise, negatively impacting prediction results.
approach: SEER proposes an augmented embedding module with mixture-of-experts and a learnable patch replacement module that dynamically filters low-quality patches and substitutes them with global series tokens via causal attention.
contribution: SEER achieves SOTA performance in robust time series forecasting through adaptive patch filtering and refinement.

problem: Existing materials discovery benchmarks evaluate isolated static tasks rather than capturing the iterative and adaptive nature of real closed-loop discovery workflows with constrained budgets.
approach: MADE formalizes materials discovery as a constrained search for thermodynamically stable compounds and provides a flexible framework where agents compose discovery components like generative models, filters, and planners.
contribution: The framework demonstrates that adaptive planning becomes more important for discovery efficiency as search space scales, validated through systematic experiments across diverse systems.

problem: Social recruitment for spatial crowdsourcing faces task heterogeneity where social influence fails to translate into physical participation, and finite task demand creates saturation traps.
approach: GKD-Recruiter models worker-task affinity via heterogeneous graphs with influential GAT, fuses signals using graph knowledge distillation, and uses Rainbow DQN to navigate non-submodular search spaces.
contribution: The method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in solution quality and inference efficiency for effective task satisfaction.

problem: Converting diffusion transformers to spiking neural networks for energy efficiency fails because standard neurons cannot accommodate the highly dynamic activation ranges across denoising steps.
approach: The framework introduces multi-threshold neurons that employ multi-level firing strategies and a membrane potential error-feedback mechanism that exploits temporal correlation between steps to recycle residual information.
contribution: The method achieves competitive generative quality on ImageNet with superior energy efficiency for spiking diffusion transformers.

problem: Existing scaling laws for LLMs fail to explain non-monotonic phenomena like catastrophic overtraining and quantization-induced degradation where performance deteriorates despite increased compute.
approach: The Shannon Scaling Law models LLM training as information transmission over a noisy channel, mapping model parameters to bandwidth and training tokens to signal power to capture learning-signal and noise interactions.
contribution: The theory outperforms classical scaling laws and predicts unseen model sizes up to 307B tokens with R²=0.847, successfully capturing non-monotonic loss basins.

problem: Block rotations for post-training quantization have limited outlier suppression because existing methods do not systematically analyze how block structure affects suppression.
approach: PeRQ introduces a greedy mass diffusion algorithm to permute activations equalizing blockwise ℓ1 norms before rotation, then merges permutations into model weights to avoid inference overhead.
contribution: The method recovers up to 90% of full-vector rotation perplexity when quantizing Llama3 1B to INT4 with block size 16, compared to 46% without permutations.

problem: Continual post-training via supervised fine-tuning leads to catastrophic forgetting of previously learned tasks, degrading both task performance and general knowledge.
approach: Reinforcement fine-tuning preserves prior knowledge through selective updates that prevent interference with established knowledge, augmented by a rollout-based instance filtering algorithm.
contribution: RFT achieves performance comparable to multi-task training while protecting general knowledge, outperforming SFT which severely degrades general capabilities.

problem: Adapting LLMs to specialized domains requires high data and computational overhead because data selection and parameter-efficient fine-tuning are treated as isolated processes.
approach: P2D identifies task-sensitive attention heads as a compass for both sample mining and structural pruning, using them to curate high-affinity data while updating only 10% of heads on 10% of data.
contribution: The method achieves 8.3 pp performance gain over baselines and delivers 7.0x end-to-end time speedup, validating parameter-data synchronization.

problem: Conformal prediction fails when labeled calibration is only available in a source domain while prediction sets are needed in a target domain without labeled calibration.
approach: TCC transports source calibration into the target space using paired data, then corrects residual mismatch using label-free uncertainty surrogates with conservative adjustment or reweighting.
contribution: The method provides finite-sample target-domain coverage guarantees that adapt to observable mismatch magnitude without labeled target calibration.

problem: Multi-view clustering struggles with view heterogeneity, noise, and ambiguous posteriors that impact both fusion reliability and clustering performance.
approach: DCL-MVC integrates contrastive learning at fusion and representation stages with fusion-then-attention for cross-view interactions, instance-level alignment, and cluster-center and prototypical contrastive losses.
contribution: The method shows consistent improvements over strong baselines across six real-world datasets with validated component contributions.

problem: Model-based reinforcement learning with MPPI relies only on sampling and neglects smooth return gradients that guide fine-grained action refinement.
approach: LaRO combines MPPI's robust global exploration with Langevin dynamics gradient refinement through a score-augmented world model, integrated via a choice mechanism called MLAP.
contribution: BOOM-L consistently outperforms strong baselines on DeepMind Control Suite and Humanoid Bench in both sample efficiency and final performance.

problem: Audio-visual LLMs process audio and video with intricate bidirectional interactions, yet their internal mechanisms for cross-modal information flow remain largely unexplored.
approach: The analysis uncovers that AVLLMs encode integrated audio-visual information in sink tokens, with a specialized subset called cross-modal sink tokens storing cross-modal information.
contribution: A training-free hallucination mitigation method encourages reliance on cross-modal sink tokens, improving generation quality.

problem: Heterogeneous federated fine-tuning with LoRA achieves only marginal savings because dense feed-forward computations dominate, and naive sparse mixture-of-experts introduces expert imbalance.
approach: UB-SMoE introduces dynamic modulated routing to rebalance expert utilization and universal pseudo-gradients to reconstruct learning signals for non-activated experts.
contribution: The method achieves up to 45.0% computational reduction on low-resource clients while improving performance by 8.7x compared to existing heterogeneous LoRA methods.

problem: Speech restoration with mismatched input-output sampling rates fails because existing methods assume matched rates and apply redundant resampling, limiting native multi-rate processing.
approach: TF-Restormer formulates the extended sampling-frequency-independent setting and proposes query-based modeling that encodes input band and synthesizes unobserved high-frequency via extension queries.
contribution: The unified model attains balanced fidelity-perceptual quality without redundant resampling across multiple benchmarks and sampling rates.

problem: Generative models for sparse field reconstruction must handle high frequency, sparsity, and dimensionality while maintaining uncertainty quantification.
approach: RP Flow applies flow matching with neural implicit functions using random Fourier features to learn signal representations queryable at arbitrary locations, with Bayesian posterior via GP regression.
contribution: The framework generates realistic samples with calibrated uncertainty estimates under challenging conditions of high frequency and sparsity.

problem: Text-to-image models relying on single-pass generation fail to handle complex prompts requiring iterative refinement and multi-round visual generation.
approach: R³-Refiner introduces the reason-reflect-rectify loop with group relative policy optimization and hierarchical reward mechanism to align rectification with reflective reasoning.
contribution: The method achieves +12.0% in reflective verdict score and +9.0% in rectification score on R³-Bench, seamlessly integrating with various MLLMs.

problem: Bayesian optimization lacks principled stopping rules that balance solution quality and evaluation cost without heuristic tuning.
approach: The method proposes a cost-aware stopping rule grounded in Pandora's Box Gittins Index and log expected improvement per cost, adapting to varying evaluation costs.
contribution: The policy provides finite-sample guarantees bounding cost-adjusted simple regret and usually matches or outperforms other acquisition-stopping pairs.

problem: Online consumer utility maximization with strategic agents fails due to strong impossibility results when using traditional value-based predictions.
approach: The mechanism uses predictions of agent identity rather than values, enabling a deterministic truthful mechanism adapted from offline randomized techniques.
contribution: The mechanism achieves constant approximation to optimal solutions under correct predictions and robust approximation under arbitrarily bad predictions.

problem: Diffusion model latent spaces are high dimensional and not explicitly organized for interpretation or controllable generation.
approach: ConDA applies contrastive learning to pretrained diffusion latents using auxiliary variables to learn low-dimensional embeddings whose directions align with dynamical factors.
contribution: The method yields more interpretable and controllable latent structure across diverse domains including fluid dynamics and neural recordings.

problem: LLM confidence estimates may violate monotonicity assumptions with human-disagreement risk and lack explicit generalization analysis.
approach: A dedicated confidence estimator uses simulated annotator diversity and margin-based ranking to model how confidently an LLM distinguishes between human-agreement and disagreement cases.
contribution: The learned estimator yields improved ranking accuracy and higher success rates in satisfying target agreement levels across datasets and models.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP remain vulnerable to adversarial examples despite zero-shot generalization, and existing test-time defenses are slow and task-specific.
approach: CSR uses spectral-guided contrastive objectives to optimize rectification perturbations realigning inputs with natural manifolds, applied input-adaptively.
contribution: CSR outperforms SOTA by an average of 18.1% against strong APGD with modest overhead and exhibits broad applicability across diverse visual tasks.

problem: Quadratic attention cost limits long-context LLM scalability on memory-constrained hardware, and static sparse methods cannot adapt to task or input variations.
approach: DHSA performs hierarchical routing estimating chunk-level importance and propagating to token interactions, maintaining causally important dependencies while enabling efficient sparsification.
contribution: The method maintains near-dense accuracy at high sparsity, achieving 12-20% relative gains over block sparse attention and 10x prefill speedup at 128K context.

problem: Task-vector-based model merging suffers from severe performance degradation due to task conflict, and existing mitigation requires costly validation-data hyperparameter tuning.
approach: OPIC formulates merging as an optimization preserving in-context learning capabilities using hierarchical refinement operators and self-generated data.
contribution: The method achieves 80.73% average performance retention, outperforming SOTA and improving by 11.1% over validation-free approaches.

problem: Learning robust human-activity representations from wearable accelerometers is constrained by scarce labeled data, and existing self-supervised methods treat streams as unstructured.
approach: A novel tokenization strategy grounds tokens in submovement theory of motor control, pretraining via masked reconstruction of movement segments using transformer encoders.
contribution: Representations pretrained on NHANES (~28k hours; ~11k participants) outperform self-supervised baselines across six subject-disjoint HAR benchmarks.

problem: Multi-agent debate evaluations using binary correctness obscure how agents revise answers during social interaction, limiting understanding of when debate helps.
approach: Analysis of ConceptARC reveals systematic distance-aware revision dynamics: agents are more likely to revise incorrect answers farther from ground truth, with revisions contracting toward truth.
contribution: The work shows structured, distance-dependent movements in solution space under social pressure, clarifying when interaction improves, stabilizes, or degrades quality.

problem: Why deep learning provides computational advantages over shallow methods remains unclear in the context of learning compositional target functions.
approach: Three-layer networks trained via layer-wise spectral estimators reveal that compositional structure allows learning in stages, reducing to simpler spectral problems.
contribution: The analysis demonstrates sharp sample-complexity separations between two and three-layer strategies, grounded in Gaussian universality.

problem: Constrained online convex optimization must minimize cumulative loss while satisfying time-varying constraints without heuristic tuning.
approach: CLASP introduces convex losses and squared penalties with variants handling joint or separate decision set and constraints, leveraging cutter operators and contraction properties.
contribution: For strongly convex problems, both algorithms provide first logarithmic guarantees on regret and cumulative squared penalty: O(log T).

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation for long-context QA is bottlenecked by expensive prefilling of large retrieved contexts, requiring selective KV recomputation.
approach: InfoFlow KV casts recomputation as an information flow problem, using attention-norm signals under inference-consistent RoPE geometry to identify effective tokens.
contribution: The method demonstrates consistent gains over prior heuristic methods under comparable latency on LLM and vision-language benchmarks.

problem: Dynamic sparse training converges significantly slower than dense training because batch normalization adversely affects sparse networks.
approach: SparseOpt proposes a sparsity-aware optimizer addressing normalization-induced gradient skew in sparse training.
contribution: Experiments on ResNet models show consistently faster convergence and improved generalization, highlighting normalization-sparsity interactions.

problem: Model merging enables unauthorized recomposition of released weights bypassing safety alignment or licensing, creating a governance gap.
approach: Trap² encodes protection into updates during fine-tuning using weight re-scaling as a proxy, keeping weights effective standalone but degrading under merging re-scaling.
contribution: The architecture-agnostic framework works across diverse architectures and release formats, protecting against unauthorized weight recomposition.

problem: Post-training data selection requires principled dataset-level selection under cost and licensing constraints, yet gradient alignment scores ignore redundancy.
approach: A scalable convex method based on kernel mean matching in gradient space jointly accounts for task alignment and cross-dataset redundancy.
contribution: The approach consistently outperforms baselines across diverse post-training settings with low computational overhead.

problem: Protein automodeling from cryo-EM density maps faces challenges in enforcing physicochemical validity and managing conformational heterogeneity.
approach: CryoACE uses atom-centric reconstruction sampling density at atomic coordinates and recycling iteratively, with training-free guidance via predicted local resolution.
contribution: The method outperforms baselines on static benchmarks and for the first time unveils atomic-level dynamic conformations on complex real-world datasets.

problem: Self-rewarding reinforcement learning suffers from systemic bias where models over-reward high-confidence mistakes, forming a self-confirming loop.
approach: RLER aggregates diverse models with adaptive reward interpolation and disagreement-aware rollout selection to reduce coupling and suppress over-reward drift.
contribution: The method improves by 6.2% over best RLIR baseline and achieves 3.6% of RLVR while exhibiting stable scaling on unlabeled data.

problem: Counterfactual explanations on tabular data are unreliable in low-density regions where classifiers exhibit high variance under model multiplicity.
approach: DensityFlow constructs robust counterfactuals via continuous-time dynamics guided by differentiable density scores to avoid uncertain regions.
contribution: The method achieves superior validity under model multiplicity while significantly reducing query costs compared to ensemble-based baselines.

problem: Sepsis prediction requires models integrating heterogeneous structured evidence from EHRs while tracking clinical deterioration over time.
approach: PathwayLLM grounds prediction on temporal signals, graph-structured evidence, and pathway-level signals, encoding observations from multiple views injected into pretrained language models.
contribution: On MIMIC-IV, the method achieves AUROC 0.891 and AUPRC 0.724, outperforming baselines with clinically relevant explanations.

problem: LLM agents require memory systems efficiently managing historical experiences to support long-term interaction without redundancy or high token costs.
approach: SimpleMem proposes semantic lossless compression with three stages: structured compression into compact indexed units, online synthesis eliminating redundancy, and intent-aware retrieval.
contribution: The method improves F1 by average 26.4% on LoCoMo while reducing inference token consumption by up to 30x.

problem: Graph anomaly detection methods rely on homophily assumptions that fail with edge heterophily, degrading performance in heterophilic graphs.
approach: HSMAD uses heterophily-weighted spectral filtering to reconstruct Laplacians and routes messages to appropriate manifolds for curvature-adaptive learning.
contribution: The method achieves state-of-the-art performance with average F1-Macro improvements of 2.66% over best-performing methods.

problem: Publishing LLM benchmarks risks test-set overfitting and evaluation gaming through feedback loops and leakage without fully disclosing ground-truth answers.
approach: CapBencher publishes benchmarks with reduced Bayes accuracy by injecting randomness through multiple logically correct answers, offering a test for leakage.
contribution: The approach accurately detects test-set overfitting across benchmarks, models, and scenarios with theoretical and empirical validation.

problem: 3D object segmentation in complex point clouds without scene-level annotations requires strong object priors for identifying multi-class objects.
approach: FoundObj uses a superpoint-based agent merging neighboring superpoints guided by semantic and geometric reward modules leveraging self-supervised foundation models.
contribution: The method outperforms baselines with strong generalization in zero-shot and long-tail scenarios for scalable label-free 3D segmentation.
